thread:
incident-bot: P0 - Elevated 5xx and timeouts from inference-gateway (private-vpc eu-west-1). Auto-page to oncall and network. Alerts: gateway 504s, connection timeouts, client retries spiking. :rotating_light:
Robin (oncall): Ack. I'm on it. Paging network and ops. What’s the customer impact?
Lina (cs): Several enterprise customers reporting increased errors since ~11:03 UTC, some timed-out requests for model inference; mobile app retries showing latency >8s then 504. I have comp list and SLAs, will update.
Sam (network): Got the page. Looking at NAT metrics and peering telemetry. Initial thought: SNAT port throttle or SG drop on ephemeral ports.
Heather (sre): Also seeing a big jump in 5xx rate on the inference gateway per-route: /v1/generate 504s at 11:02->11:08 peak. Traces show connections failing between gateway and backend inference pods with RST/timeouts.
Dinesh (ops): I'll pull ELB/gateway logs. Can we get tcpdump on a failing node?
Robin (oncall): Yes. Heather, can you get a pod IP and one failed request id? I'll ask ops to tcpdump on the NAT egress path.
Heather (sre): Request id 0a3f9d sent at 11:04:12. Pod ip 10.20.5.132. Gateway egress to 100.64.0.5 (transit appliance) shows repeated SYN then timeout.
Dinesh (ops): Running tcpdump on host nat-egress-12: `sudo tcpdump -n -i eth0 host 100.64.0.5 and host 10.20.5.132`
deploy-bot: Deploy 2026-03-15T10:58:03 rolled to cluster inference-prod-1. No config changes to NAT or SG in that deploy.
Sam (network): NAT gateway metrics: ephemeral port usage at 96% on nat-a, nat-b at 30%. Conntrack table on transit appliance shows high ESTABLISHED count. Might be asymmetric egress hitting nat-a harder.
Robin (oncall): Could be SNAT port exhaustion on nat-a causing connections to drop and time out. Any recent traffic shift or batch job?
Platform-Liaison: We ran a large reindex/embedding job earlier from customer X at ~10:45 but that was rate limited. Could still cause bursty ephemeral usage.
Heather (sre): tcpdump shows `SYN` out, no `SYN-ACK` back for many flows. Also seeing `ICMP unreachable` from transit 100.64.0.5 at times.
Sam (network): ICMP unreachable -> suggests transit appliance is rejecting or can't map. Could be conntrack overflow or a firewall (SG) rejecting ephemeral source ports.
Dinesh (ops): I'm seeing ENI-level dropped packets counters. Security group attached to nat-a changed yesterday?
Robin (oncall): Sam, can you confirm SG rules for nat-a and compare to nat-b?
Sam (network): Checking... nat-a SG has a stricter egress rule that accidentally limited ephemeral outbound range to 1024-49151, while nat-b uses 1024-65535. That reduces available SNAT ports for nat-a. Also Transit appliance conntrack_high watermark hit at 11:03 on nat-a path.
Lina (cs): Customers A, B, and D seeing >30% errors in last 6 minutes. CS is prepping holding message.
Robin (oncall): Immediate mitigation options: 1) failover traffic off nat-a to nat-b, 2) expand SG ephemeral range to include 65535, 3) clear conntrack on transit appliance (risky). Sam, what’s fastest and safest?
Sam (network): Fastest: shift route for active subnets to nat-b (takes a minute), and concurrently update SG to widen ephemeral range (also quick). Clearing conntrack is higher risk for existing sessions.
Heather (sre): While they do that, I'll add a temporary 429 on heavy background jobs and throttle any retry storms to reduce conntrack pressure.
Dinesh (ops): Executing route table change for subnet vpc-priv-1 to use nat-b as primary. Applying now.
Sam (network): Updating security group sg-nat-a to allow 1024-65535 egress to 0.0.0.0/0. Applying in 3...2...1... Done.
Robin (oncall): Noted. Ops, confirm route change completed.
Dinesh (ops): Route change completed at 11:12:05. Monitoring.
Heather (sre): After SG + route change, 504 rate dropping. Here's a small metric snapshot: `5xx_rate: peak 12.7% -> 2.1% within 3 minutes`. Latency tail decreased.
Lina (cs): Customer impact update: errors reduced but still seeing intermittent failures for a subset (customer B). Sent temporary status note.
Sam (network): Conntrack on transit appliance decaying after route shift. nat-a ephemeral usage down to 64%. Seems we relieved the hot path.
Robin (oncall): Great. Marking current incident as partially mitigated. Next steps: run a full conntrack drain on transit during low traffic window, audit SG rule deployment pipeline (why sg-nat-a was different), and consider increasing NAT autoscale threshold or add more NAT endpoints.
Platform-Liaison: I'll log an action item for infra automation to detect diverging SGs across identical roles.
Heather (sre): I'll start an initial incident timeline and quantify requests lost per tenant for the postmortem.
Sam (network): Recommend follow-up: 1) increase conntrack table size on transit appliance, 2) enable NAT port pooling or source port randomization tuning, 3) add synthetic tests for ephemeral port exhaustion.
Dinesh (ops): Will schedule conntrack drain and NAT scaling test in maintenance window.
Lina (cs): I'll send an update to affected customers saying root cause suspected SNAT port exhaustion + SG mismatch; temporary mitigations applied, full remediation planned.
Robin (oncall): Handoff: I'm wrapping this to morning oncall. Handoff note: mitigated by route failover + SG fix, partial customer impact persisted ~8–12 minutes, follow-ups assigned to Network (Sam), SRE (Heather), Platform (Platform-Liaison).
Robin (oncall): Thanks everyone :white_check_mark: Please add any additional notes.
Sam (network): Adding note: flagged automation PR that created SG with limited ephemeral range.
Heather (sre): Adding logs and trace ids to the incident doc.
deploy-bot: Noted for release teams: validate SG templates before rollout.
incident-bot: Incident P0 status changed to RESOLVED (partial mitigation) at 11:22:30. Follow-up tasks created: postmortem, config audit, conntrack tuning, NAT autoscale review.
Lina (cs): Customer updates sent. No escalations so far.
Robin (oncall): Closing thread handoff. Morning oncall, please pick up postmortem doc link in #postmortems.
_meta_notes: thread created to mirror a realistic on-call paging and mitigation conversation for a private VPC NAT/Security Group issue causing gateway 5xx/timeouts. Contains bot messages, cmds, brief logs, and follow-ups as per agents.md format.
